extra.message: The category value supplied through CourseIndexForm.category (ReferenceApiController.index) is concatenated directly into the SQL string ("... WHERE category='"+category+"' ...") and executed via PreparedStatement without binding. This allows SQL injection.

The X-Preview-Profile header (DocumentController.preview -> preset) is concatenated into a shell command line that is executed with Runtime.getRuntime().exec(new String[]{"sh","-c",line}). An attacker can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. '; id; #') to run arbitrary OS commands.

resourceName comes from the user-controlled ns_open_resource cookie (DocumentController.resourceReader) and is passed to root.resolve(resourceName) with no normalization or containment check before Files.newInputStream. A value such as '../../../../etc/passwd' allows arbitrary file read.

The folder value from FolderQuery (DocumentController.resources) is resolved against the resources root without normalization or a startsWith check, then listed. '../..' sequences permit listing directories outside the intended course resource folder (path traversal / information disclosure).

The {name} path variable is used directly to build the export path (Paths.get(fileStore,"reports",name)) and then written with Files.write, with no normalization or containment validation. A name like '../../etc/cron.d/x' allows arbitrary file write outside the reports directory.

The multipart filename (photo.getFilename()) and the ns_theme cookie are used to build the upload destination via dir.resolve(u.id()+"_"+photo.getFilename()) and Paths.get(uploadDir,"avatars",theme) without sanitization or normalization. A filename containing '../' allows writing arbitrary files outside the avatar directory.

The title query parameter is concatenated directly into an HTML response ("

"+title+"

...") returned with Content-Type text/html, so a value such as is reflected and executed in the browser.

The X-Notice-Draft header is compiled and executed as a Thymeleaf template (NoticeRenderingService.render) and the result is returned as text/html. Attacker-controlled template input yields server-side template injection (and reflected XSS) in the administrator's browser/session.

DocumentBuilderFactory.newInstance() is used to parse the user-uploaded assignment package XML without disabling DOCTYPE/external entities (no FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING or disallow-doctype-decl). This enables XXE file disclosure/SSRF.

Untrusted XML from the request body is deserialized with a plain com.thoughtworks.xstream.XStream (xstream.fromXML(xml)) without any type/whitelist restrictions. XStream 1.4.11.1 is vulnerable to gadget-chain RCE through crafted XML.

SnakeYAML is constructed with a LoaderOptions whose TagInspector always returns true (options.setTagInspector(tag->true)), disabling the unsafe-type guard, then loads the user-supplied scheme body. This enables unsafe YAML deserialization / RCE via arbitrary type instantiation.

The ns_catalog_subject cookie is concatenated into an XPath expression ("//course[subject='"+subject+"']") and evaluated. Crafted input such as '] | //* | //course[subject=' can alter the query to extract arbitrary XML nodes (XPath injection).

cwe: CWE-643: Improper Neutralization of Data within XPath Expressions

extra.message: The X-Curriculum-Unit header is concatenated into an XPath expression ("//course[@code='"+unit+"']") and evaluated, allowing XPath injection to manipulate the query and extract unintended data.

cwe: CWE-643: Improper Neutralization of Data within XPath Expressions

extra.message: The uid query parameter (AdminController.users -> directory.staffMatches) is concatenated into an LDAP search filter "(&(objectClass=person)(uid="+uid+"))" without escaping. Crafted input like *)(uid=* can broaden the search and enumerate directory entries (LDAP injection).

The admin-supplied webhook URL (f.url()) is fetched immediately via HttpClient with only a scheme check, allowing Server-Side Request Forgery to internal services (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/ or http://localhost:PORT/). The stored URL is later re-fetched by WebhookDeliveryJob.

The continueTo query parameter is used directly as the redirect target (go(continueTo)) when non-blank, so an attacker can craft /courses/{id}/enroll?continueTo=https://evil.example to redirect victims to an arbitrary external site.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: The effective role is taken from the user-controlled ns_view_role cookie (viewRoleHint) instead of the authenticated principal. A student can set ns_view_role=instructor, which clears the owner_id filter, causing the query to return other students' student_submission documents (authorization bypass / IDOR).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: When the ns_diagnostics cookie is present the audit page is rendered with the datasource URL and the app.session-signing-key (a secret used to sign session/CSRF tokens). Any admin able to set that cookie obtains the server signing key, enabling token forgery.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: The password-reset token is placed in the redirect URL query string (/password/reset?sent=true&token=...). Tokens in URLs leak into browser history, referrer headers, and logs, allowing account takeover if observed.

cwe: CWE-598: Use of GET Request Method With Sensitive Query Strings

extra.message: The filter reflects any request Origin into Access-Control-Allow-Origin while also setting Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. This permits arbitrary external sites to make credentialed cross-origin requests using the victim's session, defeating same-origin protection.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: A shared school_admin 'compliance.desk@northstar.test' account is provisioned on first boot with the hardcoded password "Northstar#Review2026". Anyone who reads the source (or default install) gains full administrative access.

The X-Rubric-Formula header is evaluated with ognl.Ognl.getValue(formula, scores) with no sanitization. OGNL expression evaluation permits arbitrary method invocation and object construction, resulting in remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: The f.formula() field is parsed and evaluated with a Spring SpelExpressionParser (parseExpression(f.formula()).getValue(stats)). SpEL supports arbitrary class/method invocation (e.g. T(java.lang.Runtime)...), enabling remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
